Fit GEV distribution using L-moments (Hosking 1990)

Source: R/hazard_validation.R
fit_gev_lmom.Rd

Estimates GEV parameters (location \(\mu\), scale \(\sigma\), shape \(\xi\)) using the method of L-moments. This is more robust than MLE for small samples (n < 50) and requires no optimization. The sign convention follows the standard meteorological form: \(\xi > 0\) = heavy tail (Frechet), \(\xi < 0\) = bounded tail (Weibull), \(\xi = 0\) = Gumbel.

Usage

fit_gev_lmom(x, xi_bounds = c(-0.4, 0.5))

Arguments

x

Numeric vector of block maxima (e.g., annual maxima).

xi_bounds

Numeric vector of length 2; allowed range for shape parameter. Default c(-0.5, 0.5) prevents extreme tail behavior.

Value

A list with elements:

mu

Location parameter.

sigma

Scale parameter.

xi

Shape parameter.

n

Sample size.

l_moments

Named vector of L1, L2, L3, tau3.

converged

Logical; whether estimation produced valid parameters.
